usual_baseline: Full protocol analgesia is uncommon: 0/27 [1517] and 34% [1321] after joint replacement. Pain was well managed in 30% [2429]. NSAIDs are under-used: 28% of eligible patients [2587], ibuprofen often omitted without a reason [1517]. IV paracetamol is used when oral would do [2587].
fix_that_works: Electronic order sets work. A prescribing order set: total compliance 0% to 58% [1517]. An EPR powerplan: 34% to 61%, with 87% of compliant patients using it [1321]. Posters and teaching: 30% more regular oral opioids on day 0 [1298].
fix_that_fails: Teaching, leaflets and emails: WHO ladder compliance fell from 83.3% to 50.9% [2020]. A departmental talk: adequate pain control only 30% to 46%, anti-emetics down from 92% to 82% [2429]. Ibuprofen stayed at 58% despite an order set [1517].
consultant_advice: Build the protocol into electronic prescribing and audit its use. Education alone has not held. More useful measures are NSAID omission without a reason and IV paracetamol when oral is possible, both simple to fix.
